items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: Monk Smith and Bill Clapinger, we used to spend most of the time standing in front of the band instead of dancing with the pretty girls.

ctx.x: To me it tells the story pretty well, those Negroid sounds. And Joe Oliver and the people who played in his style all had that particular thing, which to me is a very necessary part of jazz. That bending of notes, stretching of a note, a half tone or maybe more, stretch it as far as you can to get a blues sound. Joe Oliver had that. And he had it to such an extent that I was completely flabbergasted and spellbound. Not only was I, but Monk Smith and Bill Clapinger, we used to spend most of the time standing in…
By the way, did you ever go to Tulane or take any work up there?
